synoptic.summary: A ridge of high pressure passes overhead on Wednesday. It brings dry weather, light winds and strengthening valley inversions with haze. Wednesday is mostly cloudy (68–88% sky cover). A very weak, dry system crosses Wednesday night with no impacts expected, and Thursday is clear. On Friday a shortwave trough approaches. Flow aloft turns to 300°–315° and strengthens: 13–17 kt at about 5,500 ft above landing and 39–48 kt at about 9,500 ft. Late Friday it may bring valley rain mainly north of I-80; the launch forecasts show only 10–15% precipitation chance at 17:00 Friday. No thunderstorms are expected (thunder ≤ 1%). The daily wind cycle runs normally on Wednesday and Thursday: drainage from 110°–180° in the morning, switching to 300°–340° around 14:00. On Friday the forecast keeps 150°–170° all day with no afternoon switch. That breaks the usual pattern ahead of the approaching system.
synoptic.afd_excerpt:
Expect little
change heading into tomorrow as a ridge of high pressure slowly
passes overhead. A very weak, dry system will cross the area
Wednesday night, but is unlikely to produce any impacts.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport peaked at 1030.1 mb Tuesday morning and is now 1025.9 mb (−4.2 mb in 10 h) as the ridge axis moves through. Part of that is the normal daytime dip. Still high pressure with a light gradient, so the local daily wind cycle decides which launch works through Thursday. The fall continuing into Friday matches the approaching trough and the stronger flow aloft.

observations.summary: Newest readings are from Tuesday evening, 20:15–20:28 local. They are current at run time but about 11 h before the Wednesday morning slot. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data. In Utah Valley the evening drainage has already set in: Spanish Fork 155°/6 kt, Alpine 121°/4 kt, and Lehi at the gap 127°/11 kt (118°–171°, 4–11 kt in the last half hour). On the Salt Lake side it is nearly calm: South Valley Regional 350°/5 kt, Salt Lake airport and Provo calm. The airport forecasts call for 140°–150° at 4–5 kt overnight through 11:00 Wednesday. That agrees with the drainage seen at the gap, which is mostly below 160°.
